items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: "Big Boy" Goodie came to my hotel with some people from Switzerland and introduced me to them.

ctx.x: Another day during the week of the festival, "Big Boy" Goodie came to my hotel with some people from Switzerland and introduced me to them. One fellow's name was Peter Wydler and the other was Felix Debrit. "Big Boy" had played in Bern, Switzerland, with Glyn Pacque, the altoman I had worked with in Benny Carter's orchestra 1933 band. Pacque is mentioned in this book back in 37 or 38 and he had been able to stay in Switzerland during the war.

Peter and Felix were jazz fans and Felix advised the owner of a place in Berne called the 'Chikito' as to what jazz men should be engaged or contracted for the place. Felix wanted me to form an orchestra for an engagement in the Chikito, but he had an idea about certain American musicians whom he was in contact with, being in the orchestra. I had no great desire of becoming an orchestra leader, but "Big Boy" was helping Felix push me by telling me how nice it was to work in the Chikito. I told Felix that I would…

Don Byas, myself and the Edouard's band were no longer being booked by the Edouard 7th theater group, but someone, maybe Delaunay got us a job playing at a left bank bank club called the "Vieux Colombier" which didn't last very long and the band broke up after that engagement.
